newsitem.title: USA: Georgia jobless rate drops to 4 percent in April.
newsitem.headline: Georgia jobless rate drops to 4 percent in April.

text.p: Georgia's unemployment rate dropped to 4.0 percent in April from 4.6 percent in March and 4.3 percent a year ago, state Labor Commissioner David Poythress said.
The jobless rate was Georgia's lowest since December 1973, when it was 3.9 percent.
"Having the lowest unemployment rate we've had in Georgia in 24 years shows just how healthy our state's economy really is," Poythress said.
Georgia's jobless rate typically falls in April but this year's drop was larger than expected, possibly part of a nationwide unemployment decline in April.
"I expect only a moderate change in the unemployment rate in May, before the influx of summer job seekers begins to push the rate up in June and July," Poythress said.
Atlanta's unemployment rate dipped to 3.3 percent in April from 3.7 percent in March and 3.5 percent a year ago.
